"D" in Graham Greene's The Confidential Agent discovers a fictional Berne Manuscript of this work, while more canonical versions of this work see Jurfaleu getting his head chopped off. The cook Besgun is tasked to hold the deceitful step father of the title figure, while Bramimonde is eventually converted. The title figure is betrothed, Aude, the brother of Oliver de Vienne in it. Name this French poem about a titular horn blowing paladin of Charlemagne.

In "Desire and its Interpretation" Lacan comments on this essay and says that the phrase "inexpressibly horrible" refers to a figure's opaque sexual desire. It asks if the author of this work's subject read An Apology for Raymond Sebond, and it claims that the emotions of the titular figure are in "excess of the facts." Introducing the concept of the "objective correlative" it claims Coriolanus is an "artistic success." For 10 points – name this essay from T.S. Eliot's The Sacred Wood that deals with a certain prince of Denmark.

The title character of this work wants to have Maria Callas as a girlfriend to eat a "Compote of Apples." A couple who lived in the title hotel owned a cat named 208, and in another section a character is able to make his own reality without sugar in "The Kool-Aid Wino." Written by the author of In Watermelon Sugar, in the section "Knock On Wood" Pittsburgh is described as the Carnegie of the titular fish. For 10 points – name this abstract work, a novella by Richard Brautigan.

In one work by this author, the chairman of the I.P.H. Is declared "out of hand," but delivers the speech anyways. This author was accused of plagiarizing that speech "The Bishop's Vision" from a Frank Norris essay. He wrote an account of the plight of the Whitechapel District titled, The People of the Abyss. He described his sailing adventures in The Cruise of the Snark and his alcoholic memoirs in John Barleycorn. For 10 points – name this American author of The Iron Heel and White Fang.

This author of Sciencea and Hebrew Tradition engaged the son of Wilberforce in a debate. When asked about his lineage he replied, "I would rather be the offspring of two apes than be a man and afraid to face the truth."

The protagonist of this work leverages an interest in the works of Parker Tyler to attend parties, such as one where she passes out after mixing gin and weed and another in which a "rude intrusion" is perpetrated by one of the Four Skins. It climaxes with a scene involving Rusty Godowski, a student in the title character's Empathy and Posture classes, being anally raped with strap-on. For 10 points— name this novel with a sexually reassigned title character, a work of Gore Vidal.

A late work of this person is based on a Bill White broadcast from the Finnish front of the Winter War; an early one adapts a Ring Lardner work in which Joe Roberts throw his steward off the titular ship for spilling tea. In addition to The Love Nest and There Shall Be No Night, this writer created a work in which life insurance causes hitchhiker Alan Squier beg Duke Mantee to shoot him. For 10 points— name this author of Idiot's Delight, Abe Lincoln in Illinois, and The Petrified Forest.

This person's late career saw staging of two bureaucratic satires, The Bathhouse and The Bedbug, and publication of the travelogue My Discovery of America. This writer's earlier works "The Backbone Flute" and "Cloud in Trousers" reflect the aggressive style of "A Slap in the Face of Public Taste", to which manifesto he contributed. Love is the theme of this poet's "About This" and "I Love". For 10 points— name this author of a lengthy elegy to Lenin, a Futurist poet of the Russian Revolution.

The title character is visited by Henry Palmetto, who kills himself with a train, and Ripley Snell, whose right hand was run over by Ulysses Swett's automobile. Francis Cugat designed the cover for this novel that features a gypsy who moves her hand like a Frisco. One character plays "ONE THINGS' FOR SURE AND NOTHING'S SURER / THE RICH GET RICHER AND THE POOR GET CHILDREN," a song called "The Love Nest," while another reads The Rise and Fall of the Colored Empires. That reader breaks the nose of his mistress when they discuss whether she has any right to say his wife's name, where the McGees are in attendance and the narrator gets drunk for the second time in his life. Another character in this novel wears cuff links made of molars and rigs the 1919 World Series. West Egg is the partial setting of what Nick Carraway narrated Jazz Age novel by F. Scott Fitzgerald?

He wrote of "An Unusual Young Man" in his Letters from America. His affair with Taatamata was remembered in his "Tiare Tahiti." While living in Germany with Ka Cox, he asked "is there honey still for tea" in "The Old Vicarage, Grantchester." He later described a body "washed by the rivers, blest by the suns of home." name this poet who instructs "If I should die, think only this of me/That there's some corner of a foreign field/That is for ever England" in "The Soldier."

The author of this play was inspired to write it by a sailor known as "The Little Horse." Shortly after a man who is "the grandson of the village idiot" and has "the face of a clown" is introduced, the main character learns that the driver of a banana truck, whose ashes sit in an urn on stage, was an unfaithful drug smuggler. Name this play in which Serafina falls in love with Alvaro because he has the same mark on his chest as her late husband, a work by Tennessee Williams.

Anulka and Jacek fall in love during the second siege of Vienna in this author's On the Field of Glory. The virtuous Cossack Hmelnitski is defeated by Prince Yeremi after saving the life of Pan Yan in one of this author's novels. In another novel, the writer of the Troyad sets Rome on fire to provide better imagery, Pomponia converts Lygia to Christianity, and Petronius kills himself. Name this Polish author of With Fire and Sword and Quo Vadis?

One of his plays contains the First and Second Chaps and First and Second Sidneys, who become involved in Leopold Nettles's impending arrest for subversive writing. Dr. Balcar cries when Eduard Huml exposes the fraud of the Puzuk machine in another of his plays. In addition to Largo Desolato and The Increased Difficulty of Concentration, he wrote about a social gathering of the Liquidation Office in The Garden Party. Name this Czech dissident and politician.

This writer's poetry includes the twelve-part "Calendar of Sonnets." Animals star in her Mammy Tittleback and Her Family and Letters From a Cat, while she depicted her friend Emily Dickinson in Mercy Philbrick's Choice. Father Gaspara agrees to perofrm a marriage between the shepherd Allesandro and the biracial title character of one of her novels, who thwarts the anti-Indian Señora Moreno. Name this author of Ramona and the history of abuses towards Indians, A Century of Dishonor.

Literary critics are compared to this figure in the concluding section of Viktor Shklovsky's Third Factory. This character observes "the towers that men contrive" when he is "far from home at nightfall by the Potomac" in an Allen Tate poem that finds him "at Washington." In Troilus and Cressida, he delivers Hector's challenge to the Greek warriors. In another work, he is trapped in a cave by a storm with romantic results, and he holds funeral games for his father Anchises. Name this hero of a Roman epic.

One character's grave gets marked with a stone bearing the word "Resurgem" in this work, and another character tries to elope with Lord Edwin Vere but fails. The title character dreams at one point for seven consecutive nights about babies shortly before receiving word that her cousin has committed suicide. A wedding is ruined by Mr. Briggs revealing the job of Grace Pool. Name this work in which the death of Bertha Mason allows Mr. Rochester to marry the title character.

One character in this work takes the name John Hobbs after cudgeling a man who read stories to one of the main characters, Father Andrews. One character dreams of a dwarf showing him where to dig for 12 pennies before giving a hereditary position to Humphrey Marlow. One title character is almost killed by a hermit before returning to London with Miles Hendon. Name this work in which a poor boy and royalty exchange positions for a time, written by Mark Twain.

One work by this author describes the marriage of Katrina Taylor and Edward Dougherty along with the "Love Nest Killings of 1908", while another has the title character chasing Veronica Fitzgibbon after giving up politics under Patsy McCall. In addition to The Flaming Corsage and Roscoe, this man wrote about Bailey organizing a newspaper strike in The Ink Truck. Name this American author of works often set in Albany, New York, such as Legs and Ironweed.

One character in this work fails to sell a painting and a wall clock. Alvaro had earlier bought that character's sewing machine and worked with her son before the son was killed by the mayor's men. The title character goes to the harbor every Friday to wait for the mail and sells a rooster to Sabas before reneging on the deal. Name this work where that rooster from Agustín and a pension check serve as hope for the title character in a Gabriel García Marquez work.
No One Writes to the Colonel

One visitor to these people described them as being "like the Carolingian kings…decayed to a mere beautiful futility." That visitor would later compare these people to "mere fatted cattle" before deciding to share "in their degradation and their Fear" despite their "intellectual degradation." One member of this group is saved from drifting away by a man who loses a certain vehicle and is named Weena. Name this group paired with the Morlocks in H.G. Well's The Time Machine.

One part of this book ends with a policeman killing the child-murderer Hinzelmann. At another point in this novel, the prostitute Bilquis consumes a client. It opens with the protagonist leaving prison and finding out that his wife died while engaged in a sex act in a car with his friend Robbie. That man works for Mr. Wednesday, who is attempting to make war on airplanes and the Internet with the aid of Czernobog, Thoth, and Anansi. Name this 2001 fantasy by Neil Gaiman.

One character in this work saves a boy from an oncoming train, which causes problems with his wife Robbie. One character's mother sends handmade quilts from her shack, and that son's new home, Marmion, is prepared by his father-in-law Battle. Laura McRaven fears that she will not be accepted into the main family after arriving at the Shellmound plantation from Jackson. Name this Eudora Welty work about Troy Flavin's marriage into Dabney Fairchild's family.

The builder of an organ takes the name Silbermann to hide his identity in this work, and that character is a member of the League of Journeyers to the East, which helped society move past the Age of the Feuilleton according to Plinius Ziegenhalss. One character studies at the schools of Eschholz and Waldzell and becomes a tutor to Tito, the son of Plinio Designori, before drowning. Name this work in which Joseph Knecht becomes the Magister Ludi, a work by Herman Hesse.

The protagonist of this novel is sickened by eating dirt after a rosebush in a cave blooms in February, signifying to Peyramale that he should build a shrine. At the end of this novel, Maria Therese apologizes for her rudeness and a local atheist is converted. Opening with a cart full of amputated limbs being dumped into the Grotto of Massabielle by the title character's mother, Francois Soubirous, name this work of Franz Werfel about a religious vision in 1858 France.

One of his early plays ends with a priest being stuffed into a sack. That play about Michael Byrne and Sarah Casey, A Tinker's Wedding, followed his When The Moon is Set and was written before his version of a myth about a beautiful woman who brings grief to Naisi and Conchobar, Deirdre of the Sorrows. He also wrote about Bartley, the last son of Maurya, and Christy Mahon, who claims to have killed his father. Name this author of Riders to the Sea and A Playboy of the Western World.

In this novel, a woman stops on the way to dinner and demands that her date win six thousand francs gambling; that woman is later caught by her husband trying to sell the de Restaud family diamonds. Bianchon is one of two people at the title character's deathbed at the Maison Vauquer, after that man is unable to move into a new apartment with Eugene de Rastignac as planned. Only empty carriages are sent by Delphine and Anastasia to their father's funeral. Name this novel about an exploited Frenchman by Balzac.

The Institute of Chemistry invents a recipe for poppy-seed rolls in his story "The Needle." In a novel by him, Macedonia and Senegal invade Finland during a war that kills all but thirteen people on Earth, caused by the Karburator, an energy machine. In addition to The Absolute at Large, he wrote about Captain van Toch finding a new source of labor near Sumatra, and Dr. Gall bestowing souls upon Helena and Primus. Name this writer of War With the Newts and R.U.R.

An uncle and nephew with this surname reformed the Scottish education system and Church in the late 1500s. In addition to Andrew and James, a film by a man of this surname follows Jef Costello and uses The Book of Bushido. One work of a man by this name involves the HMS Bellipotent and Captain Edward Vere. Jean-Pierre directed films like Les Enfants Terribles and Le Samourai. Give this surname also shared with the author of Whtie-Jacket, Billy Budd and Moby Dick.

One section of this work consists of a school competition essay by its narrator, while its dialogue-only first two chapters is followed by a diary entry about the Charity Show at P.S. 3. Elsewhere, the narrator brags to the piano teacher Herminia that he reads "almost a book a day". Alan Cheuse compares it to a 1961 Walker Percy story and titles it "A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Moviegoer". Centering on the uJose Casals, aka Toto, name this first novel by Manuel Puig.

Two characters in this work make colored condoms called "O-Daddies," while Fritz constantly expounds on his religious views. In one scene, a beheaded turtle climbs to the top of a pile of decapitated animals, and it ends with the protagonist escaping to Texas after he is blinded by the legless strongman Schmidt. Centered around a chili parlor in the Hotel Crocket and Finnerty's brother and Doc's speakeasy, name this work about the hobo Dove Linkhorn, set in New Orleans, by Nelson Algren.
A Walk on the Wild Side

The coming of a "naked hulk" precedes one instance of them, and following their use, "the sun's rim dips". In a work in which the title character loves pastrami, they lead to the death of Damon Rutherford. Another work on them talks about "preparing in the fist that might clutch it". The "Nighmare-life-in Death" gains control of the Ancient Mariner with, what items that Mallarme claimed "would never abolish chance," and which figure in the "Sabha Parvan" game in the Mahabarata?

This author talks of language in "A Prayer in the Mother Tongue", and a coin-filled street in "The Money Road". He relates helping his dying grandfather urinate in "Diary of My Sixteenth Year", which appears in a collection with several of his Palm-of-Hand stories. His most famous story sees ballet critic Shimamura travel to Yuzawa to hang out with Komako, a geisha. Also penning "The Dancing Girl of Izu", name this Japanese author of The Master of Go and Snow Country.

A Puritan in this novel feels so guilty that she runs into a cathedral and confesses to a priest. That character, Hilda, eventually marries Kenyon. A character who is last seen at Raphael's tomb in the Pantheon first meets one admirer while viewing a Praxiteles statue. In this novel, the Capuchin Antonio stalk his former fiancee, a relationship that ends when the protagonist throws Antonio from the Tarpeian Rock. Miriam magically convinces Donatello to commit murder in what novel of Nathaniel Hawthorne?

One author tied up this work's ambiguous ending in the short story "The End". A son of the protagonist is given advice by Viscacha, while that character later gives better advice to his sons. The protagonist was forced into the army, which he deserts, meeting Sergeant Cruz, and he kills a black man at a dance; his son later comes back for vengeance, and the book ends before they may duel. For 10 points— name this novel about the pampas by José Hernández, a notable example of gaucho literature.

Heinrich Mann wrote an essay about him and the Crisis of Modern Thought. The title phrase of one of this author's novels is uttered by a pastor citing the book of Luke, which causes an amethyst cross to be worn by Alissa as she resists Jerome. In addition to [?] Strait is the Gate, this author wrote about Vincent being loved by Lilian Griffith in addition to having Gheridanson causing the grandchild of La Perouse, Boris, to commit suicide. In that work, Olivier's friend Bernard runs away from home when he discovers he is a bastard. In a more famous novel, the title character is an ancient history scholar that suffers from tuberculosis, who then receives a scissors from his friend Menalque that belong to Moktir. Name this author that created Michel and wrote The Counterfeiters and The Immoralist.

This author collaborated with his wife Carol Dunlop in his Autonauts of the Cosmoroute, and in one of his novels, this man had the winners of a lottery be quarantined on a cruise ship when a disease breaks out. In another novel, the message: "wake [?] up" is given to the protagonist of a novel featuring "the one I told you." In addition to writing The Winners and about "the Screwery" and Andres Fava in A Manual for Manuel, this author of Blow-up, Bestiario, and Around the Day in Eighty Worlds is best known for a novel in which Rocamadour dies and La Maga holds a funeral, the latter of which may occur first because the reader may read only the odd pages, or jump between chapters. Name this author of Hopscotch.

This author that adapted The Devil and Daniel Webster as the play Scratch imagined several couple dancing under the moonlight of the Antilles in a play in which Peter deserts Ann for Elizabeth in his The Music [?] Crept By Me on Upon the Waters. In another play, because levy for the school bond failed, Joe and Jill strive to make it pass, while another play features a woman who sings at the exact scale of a siren in a follow up to his The Fall of the City. In addition to writing The Secret of Freedom, Air Siren, and about McGafferty in Panic, this author also wrote about the title character's son David dying not in the heroics of war, but because of his careless comrades in addition to having Mary and Jonathan fatally crashing into a viaduct, in which Zuss and Nickles represent God and Devil in adaptation of the Biblical Job Story. Name this author of J.B.

This poem imagines "Enlarged winds, that curl the flood," and "The sweetness, mercy, majesty, and the glories of my King." It is set "When flowing cups run swifty round, With no allaying Thames," and the narrator will be like committed linnets when and sing "with shriller throat." It imagines "the birds that wanton in the air," and "fishes [?] that tipple in the deep." This work also pictures "Minds innocent and quiet take," "thirsty grief in wine we steep, when healths and draughts go free -." The title addressee "brings to whisper at the gates," and the speaker repeatedly uses the phrase "Know no such Liberty," except when describing "Angels alone, that soar above." Beginning by noting "Stone walls do not a prison make," name this Richard Lovelace poem written from a jail.

In one of this author's works Lady Carlotta forces her students Claude and Wilfird to re-enact the rape of the Sabine women for a history lesson in "The Schartz-Metterklume Method," while Harvey Bope gives his nephews untraditional gifts such as an action figure of John Herschel and a model of the Young Women's Christian Association in [?] "The Toys of Peace." This author wrote about Francesca discovering that her prized Van der Meulen painting is fake after learning of the death of her son Comus in The Unbearable Bassington. In one of his stories Mrs. De Ropp is killed by the animal Conradin worships as a god, and in his best known work Vera tricks Framton Nuttel with a false story about Mrs. Sappleton's lost husband to explain the titular orifice. Name this author of "Sredni Vashtar" and "The Open Window."

In one poem from this collection a figure who "raised up her head / From the darkness, dread, and drear" begs for someone to "Break this heavy chain / That does freeze my bones around" In addition to "Earth's Answer" the introductory poem of this collection discusses "The Holy Word / That walked among the ancient trees" after the opening exclamation [?] "Hear the Voice of the Bard." The speaker of another poem sees the "marks of weakness, marks of woe" in "every face" he meets while "wander[ing] thro' each chartered street" of the title city, while the speaker of the best known poem in this collection asks the titular creature "What the hammer? What the chain? / In what furnace was thy brain?" name this poetry collection including "Poison Tree", "London", and "The Tyger" written by William Blake several years after a companion collection about innocence.

In one of this author's works a prompter informs a playwright that he might find his play short because the actors have cut sections they found ‘‘heavy or unnecessary to the plot.'' He wrote about Tom Fashion's triumph over his miserly brother Lord Foppington in A Trip to Scarborough, and in another work Sir Fretful Plagiary accosts Mr. Dangle before he attends a rehearsal Mr. Puff's new play [?] The Spanish Armada. In one of his plays Crabtree and Sir Benjamin Backbite make up a false story about a nonexistent duel between Peter Teazle and Joseph before Lady Sneerwell complains that her plans to ruin the marriage Maria and Charles Surface have failed. In addition to The Critic, in his best known play Bob Acres and Lucius O'Trigger both court a woman, who is infatuated with "Ensign Beverley", who is actually Jack Absolute is disguise in his play featuring Mrs. Malaprop. Name this Irish playwright, who wrote School for Scandal and The Rivals.

After the protagonist of this novel seduces Milly, he is murdered by her grandfather Wash Jones. According to its author, this novel is about a character "who wanted sons and his sons [?] destroyed him." The final narrators of this novel eventually conclude that one of those sons was murdered because he was part black, not because he committed incest. This novel begins with Rosa Coldfield telling a story about a man who appeared from nowhere to build his namesake "hundred" to Quentin Compson, who attempts to understand why Henry killed his brother Charles Bon. Name this novel about Thomas Sutpen by William Faulkner.

This author imitated the style of Tristram Shandy in his novel The Memoirs of Herrn von Schnabelewopski, which inspired Wagner's opera The Flying Dutchman. Schumann set this author's poetry to music in A [?] Poet's Love. Ferdinand Feiligrath's poem "The Moorish Prince" inspired this author's satire about a dancing bear, "Atta Troll." This author of the poetry collections Romanzero satirized his native country in Germany: A Winter's Tale, written after his exile. His Book of Songs includes a poem about a woman whose powerful singing captivates sailors, leading to their death. Name this nineteenth century German poet of "Die Lorelei."

This author wrote about the negotiations between Matthias Erzberger and Ferdinand Foch at Versailles in one novel, while another of his works sees Anthony Piers investigate the strangulation of Victor Henneker on an Antarctic expedition. In addition to Gossip from the Forest and A Victim of the Aurora, he wrote a novel in which Usaph Bumpass and Decatur Cate serve in the forces of Stonewall Jackson, [?] Confederates. He described the "Improbable Birth of" his home country in A Commonwealth of Thieves, while one of his novels about that country sees the titular half-Aborigine flip out and kill two families after being cheated out of money. Identify this Australian author of The Chant of Jimmie Blacksmith who won the 1982 Booker Prize for a novel in which a dude saves a bunch of Jews, Schindler's Ark.

Its epigraph, adapted from Horace, notes that "nevertheless foot and head are assigned to a single shape", while its title page claims it to be a translation by "William Marshal" from the original by "Onuphrio Muralto". Near this work's end, one character's ghost is accepted into heaven by St. Nicholas. One character finds a prophetic weapon in the Holy Land that leads him to disguise himself as the Knight of the [?] Gigantic Sabre and return to the title location. Father Jerome, the former Prince of Falconara, discovers that its protagonist is his son; that protagonist, Theodore, is aided by Matilda and eventually marries Isabella. At the beginning of this novel, Conrad is crushed by the colossal helmet of Alfonso the Good, leading his usurping father Manfred to search for a new heir. Identify this first Gothic novel, a work of Horace Walpole.

In one novel, this author wrote about Hendrik's mistress driving Magda insane, while in another Sergey Nechayev has many conversations with Pavel's stepfather, Fyodor Dostoyevsky. In addition to In [?] the Heart of the Country, and The Master of Petersburg, the title character of another novel ponders over "A Modest Proposal," wondering if it's wrong to eat babies, why is it not wrong to eat pigs? In another work, the unnamed narrator journeys across the desert to deliver a blind girl to the title folk only for him, The Magistrate, to be captured by Colonel Joll. In addition to Elizabeth Costello and Waiting for the Barbarians, a professor working on Lord Byron is seduced by Melanie, leading him, David Lurie, to be fired. Name this author of Disgrace, a notably South African author.

This is the moniker of the woman who relates the poem "touissant," in for colored girls by Ntozake Shange, as well as the last name of Betsy, her only novel's title character. It is the last name of the author of a novel featuring Eliza [?] Holmes exposing Harriot Fawcet's boyfriend as her brother. A character of this last name betrays Dion Anthony and lover her brother Margaret in a play with this adjective in its title. In addition to the last name of the author of The Power of Sympathy, and it being the last name of the author of Arthur Mervyn and Wieland, it is the last name of Billy in Eugene O'Neill's play with this word in its title along with "Great and "God." This is the last name of a man who ventures into the forest with the devil to initiate a ritual with his wife Faith. Give this last name of "Young Goodman," in a story by Nathaniel Hawthorrne.

One character in this work describes how "no one passes up" the opportunity to lap at a bowl of rice pudding, and that character earlier stuffed a pair of ladies' handkerchiefs into his collar. The impetus for the events of this story lies in one character threatening to "eat" his master "up" after failing to salute at the stroke of two. The [?] Soldier accidentally tears a leather wrist strap, prompting another character to replace it with a chain while continually complaining about the New Commandant. It ends with the Officer replacing the Condemned Man in the Harrow and dying as "Be Just" is inscribed upon his body. Identify this short story in which the Traveller observes the use of a torture machine, a work of Franz Kafka.

This character is influenced by a scientific theory asserting mankind was created from slime in a series of three spontaneous generations put forth by the Professor of Natural History Dom Antonio José Kuckuck. He looks for a peculiar store called "Ladder to Heaven Street" to sell some of the jewels he stole while going through customs from Madame Houpfle, and he left his sister Olympia after his champagne making father Engelbert committed suicide. This character is inspired by watching the actor [?] Muller Rose take off his makeup and while he was working as a waiter at the Hotel Saint James and Albany in Paris he uses the name Armand. Assuming the identity of the Marquis de Venosta, the subtitle of this character's titular novel is "Confidence Man." name this character whose "Confessions" were written by Thomas Mann in a 1954 novel.

A character that committed suicide in a later work of this work's author was described in this work as having "the melancholy air and intellectual abstraction of a Hamlet". The title character, once seen "a-talking to a jaybird", enjoys listening to a song about "the Arethusa, Seventy-four" sung by the sailor "Man-o'-War Jack". A "noted wag" named "Boston" arranges a satire of a church service in this work, but that is stopped when [?] Stumpy declares himself godfather and christens the title character "Thomas". This story ends when a flood kills both Kentuck and the title character, who'd been nursed by a donkey. Identify this story in which Cherokee Sal dies while giving birth to the title character, a work of Bret Harte.

One character in this play returns from a trip promoting her acting career horrified that there is a toilet backstage at the Lyceum in Rochester. Another character claims she was late because she was picking a bundle of flowers, which she actually found in the garbage can, and the first act begins with Peggy Roger's recitation of The Merchant of Venice "quality of mercy" speech. [?] In the third act Lily Mortar returns after avoiding testifying in a court case and Dr. Joseph Cardin tries to convince the main character to leave for Austria with him. In this play one character uses the stolen bracelet of Helen Burton to blackmail Rosalie Wells into making a false confession that leads to the shutdown of the Wright-Dobie School for Girls. Name this play in which Mary Tilford accuses her teachers Karen Wright and Martha Dobie of having a lesbian romance, by Lillian Hellman.

One of his works describes religion as a "moth-eaten musical brocade/created to pretend we never die" after noting that "the mind blanks at the glare". That work by this man describes "postmen like doctors" going "from house to house" and begins "I work all day, and get half-drunk at night". The speaker of another of his poems glosses over the "plainness of the pre-Baroque" before seeing a pair of stone figures holding hands and averring that they "prove our almost-instinct almost true: What will survive of us is love." His collections include The [?] Whitsun Weddings and High Windows, the latter of which contains a poem that notes that misery "deepens like a coastal shelf" and advises the listener to "Get out as early as you can". Identify this 20th-century British poet of "Aubade" and "An Arundel Tomb", who described the effects of "your mum and dad" rather graphically in his "This Be the Verse".

This author asserted that "The trees must form ranks to keep the giant with seven-league boots from passing!" and noted that "The conceited villager believes the entire world to be his village" in one work. In another work, he wrote that he cultivated "neither nettles nor thorns" for the "cruel person/who tears out the heart with which I live"; rather, he cultivates the titular [?] "White Rose". This author wrote the aforementioned essay Our America and saw Jose Fernandez adapt a poem from his Versos Sencillos into the patriotic song "Guantanamera". Identify this author of the collection Versos Libres, who died at the Battle of Dos Rios fighting for the independence of his home country, Cuba.

This work is preceded by an "Author's Preface" written from Shawmut College, and the first chapter of the work proper contains an extended metaphor in which a "prodigious coach" driven by hunger represents society. Its sequel, which contains the "parable of the water tank", is called Equality. Its protagonist's servant, Sawyer, dies in a fire, preventing him from [?] waking the protagonist from Dr. Pillsbury's hypnosis. This novel describes how all citizens spend three years after age 21 doing menial labor in service of the "Great Trust", which has replaced all private monopolies. Its protagonist eventually falls in love with a descendent of Edith Bartlett, the daughter of Dr. Leete. Identify this novel about Julian West's adventures in a circa-2000 socialist utopian U.S.A., a work of Edward Bellamy.

This author wrote about two friends climing Mount Aso in The 210th Day and collected a series of vignettes in his Ten Nights of Dreams, while his novel The Miner is discussed by Oshima and Kafka in a Haruki Murakami work. One of his works sees the principal Badger manipulated by Red Shirt, who gets beaten up by Porcupine and the title character, a math teacher on Shikoku. The narrator of another of his works is finally able to paint O-Nami Shioda after she gains compassion. His best-known work sees [?] Mr. Sneaze attempt to arrange the marriage of Opula Goldfield and Avalon Coldmoon before its narrator drowns in a water barrel.
